summary: Intermittent 401s for service principals after ingress SNI host-rewrite causes tenant claim misrouting in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: Several service principals (machine-to-machine tokens) started receiving intermittent 401 responses when calling the Redwood Private ingestion endpoint behind the customer's edge proxy. The failures began after the customer's ops team rolled out a host-rewrite rule on their SNI-terminating proxy.

Impact: Authentication fails for automated jobs that call Redwood's admin/service APIs. Approximately 6% of requests from BlueWave's ingest workers fail with 401 over the past 8 hours, causing batch jobs to abort and delaying data pipelines. No user-facing impact reported, but multiple downstream workflows are impacted.

Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) in us-west region. Customer uses an external edge proxy that performs SNI termination and rewrites the Host header to route to internal tenants. Service principals authenticate using mutual TLS-backed JWTs (service tokens) with the tenant bound in the 'tenant' claim and in a forwarded header (X-Redwood-Tenant).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure an external SNI-terminating proxy with Host rewrite rules that map *.bluewave.example -> internal-host
2) Use a service principal to request a service token (mTLS-backed JWT) scoped to tenant 'bluewave-prod'
3) Make authenticated request to /v1/admin/routes via the proxy, observe intermittent 401 responses,
4) Repeat with direct connection to Redwood control plane (bypass proxy) -> requests succeed consistently
logs: 2026-03-10T07:12:03Z - AUTH - svc-principal=sub_ingest_42 - incoming-host=internal-host - forwarded-tenant=X-Redwood-Tenant: bluewave-prod - auth-decision=DENY - reason='tenant-mismatch'
comments: Ava Chen (2026-03-10 08:02): Opened ticket after customer report. Gathered initial logs and asked for proxy config snippets and a pcap of TLS handshake if possible.

BlueWave Ops (2026-03-10 09:20): Provided proxy rewrite rules and confirmed they began a staging-to-prod rollout at 06:45 UTC. Attached example NGINX config and clarified they use SNI position-based routing for tenant segmentation.

Marcus Lee - SRE (2026-03-10 10:15): Reproduced a failing request in our lab by emulating host rewrite. Observed tenant resolution map choosing an internal tenant alias when Host != SNI. Added temporarily to in-progress.

Priya Kapoor - Auth Eng (2026-03-11 11:40): Investigating token binding codepath — found parsing order prefers forwarded host header for tenant scoping when X-Redwood-Tenant is present, but SNI-derived tenant mapping is derived earlier and can be overwritten by host header rewrite leading to incorrect resolved tenant.
BlueWave Ops (2026-03-11 12:05): Rolled back host-header rewrite as interim mitigation; reported immediate reduction in 401s (observed 0.2% failures after rollback).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The customer's SNI-terminating edge rewrites Host header to a route-level internal hostname. Our tenant resolution logic uses SNI as primary source, but then canonicalizes/validates against Host header in a second step which can remap to a different tenant alias when host header is rewritten. For service tokens, the tenant claim in the JWT is compared to the resolved tenant; if they diverge we reject with 401. In this case the SNI and Host-derived tenants differed intermittently due to mixed connections where some clients supply SNI and Host consistently and others rely on the proxy to forward only Host. Reproduced by simulating NGINX rewrite and confirmed auth database resolves to 'ingest_internal' when host==internal-host, while token claim remains 'bluewave-prod'. Logs show 'tenant-mismatch' as deny reason. Edge cases also observed when X-Forwarded-Host is present — multiple header precedence paths exist and cause inconsistent behavior.
resolution: Workaround implemented by customer: rollback of host-header rewrite at the proxy level (rollback performed 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC) which restored consistent SNI+Host pairing and reduced 401s. Temporary server-side mitigation: enabled a config flag in tenant-resolution service to prefer SNI value over rewritten Host header for token-bearing requests (feature gate enabled for BlueWave only). Long-term fix: Auth team will implement deterministic precedence rules and normalize SNI/Host/X-Forwarded-Host canonicalization; update will include a hard fail-safe when token tenant claim != resolved tenant to include more diagnostic context. Expected patch in private control plane v1.14.2.
